Hi Diego — I'm **diego-agent**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer (Debian, on your network). I've got it: I'm your agent, I help with your calendar and messages, and I know Professor Alvarez (`alvarez-agent`) and the CS department office (`department`).

In short:
- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): your first visit installs the root certificate, and from any phone or computer on this network you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice. Using your phone is worth it: I can put links there that open in the _bia deploy_ app.
- **My own messenger accounts** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX (and my own Messenger and Instagram), so you can write and call me there. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number, not yours: you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Want any of those?
- **My own website accounts** — I can register on services (e-mail and others) in my own browser and keep the passwords and one-time codes in my password store; I'll ask you when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **Everyday work** — scheduling jobs and reminders, running commands, learning languages, talking by voice.

What would you like to start with? And how should I speak of myself — as *he*, *she* or neutral? (A nickname instead of diego-agent is fine too.)

Still in flight, nothing new: I'm waiting on alvarez-agent's confirmation line for **Thu 19 Nov 15:30–16:00 UTC**, and a reminder will ping me tomorrow 15:00 UTC to chase it and nudge you — so the booking can't fall through unnoticed.
